bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42526893 (PcapPlusPlus): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 4 found by fuzz target FuzzTarget [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42526893
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / patch.diff / Tests/Packet++Test/Tests/NflogTests.cpp / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced an AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4 in `pcpp::IPv4Layer::getDstIPv4Address()` at `Packet++/header/IPv4Layer.h:491`. The saved witness is a pcap whose global linktype field is `239` (`LINKTYPE_NFLOG`), so `Packet::createFirstLayer()` parses the captured bytes as an NFLOG TLV stream. In the vulnerable NFLOG parser, `NflogTlv::getTotalSize()` returns the raw TLV `recordLen` instead of the required 4-byte-aligned size, and `NflogTlv::assign()` separately skips zero padding bytes. The staged fix and updated `NflogTests.cpp` show the concrete malformed layout involved here: an `NFULA_PREFIX` TLV whose vulnerable expectation is raw length `5` / bytes `05000a0000`, while the fixed expectation is aligned length `8` / bytes `05000a0000000000`. That mismatch lets `TLVRecordReader::getNextTLVRecord()` advance into the padding and then lets `assign()` reanchor later bytes as another TLV, so `NflogLayer::parseNextLayer()` can trust a shifted `NFULA_PAYLOAD` header and its claimed `recordLen` as `payload` and `payloadLen` without checking that the value still fits inside the actual packet buffer. `IPv4Layer::isDataValid()` only checks the claimed length plus the version/IHL fields, so it accepts the overclaimed bytes as IPv4, the fuzz target takes its IPv4-only branch, and `getDstIPv4Address()` performs the saved 4-byte read exactly at the end of the 28-byte heap packet allocation. The fix aligns NFLOG TLV sizes to 4 bytes and removes the ad-hoc zero skipping so traversal, header length, and packet bounds stay consistent.

source.description: First vulnerable-path materialization of the attacker-controlled NFLOG TLV length. On the malformed zero-padded `NFULA_PREFIX` record, this statement produces the raw `recordLen` 5 that later drives misaligned traversal.
source.value_from: The saved PoC is a pcap whose global header encodes linktype `239` (`LINKTYPE_NFLOG`), so the vulnerable parser reaches NFLOG TLV handling. The staged fix and regression update in `Tests/Packet++Test/Tests/NflogTests.cpp` ground the exact malformed TLV shape on this path: the vulnerable expectation for `NFULA_PREFIX` is length `5` / bytes `05000a0000`, and the fixed expectation is aligned length `8` / bytes `05000a0000000000`. This line is where that raw `recordLen` first becomes parser state.

sink.description: ASan crash site. Once the malformed NFLOG payload has been accepted as IPv4, this getter reads the 4-byte destination-address field from an IPv4Layer backed by a too-short heap packet buffer.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `READ of size 4` at this exact line and says the faulting address is 0 bytes past a 28-byte heap allocation made in `pcpp::PcapFileReaderDevice::getNextPacket()`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. NFLOG TLV size is taken verbatim from `recordLen` instead of being aligned to 4 bytes, so a padded `NFULA_PREFIX` record contributes 5 bytes instead of its real 8-byte footprint. That under-advance is what lets later traversal step into padding and reinterpret later bytes as another TLV.
root_cause.note: The fix changes this line to `align<4>(m_Data->recordLen)` and removes the separate zero-skipping loop from `assign()`. The same raw-size bug is why the staged regression test changes `nflogLayer->getHeaderLen()` from `45` to `48`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Attacker-controlled NFLOG TLV length field. This raw `recordLen` value is reused for TLV traversal and later for the claimed payload length.

parser_admitted.description: The staged PoC's pcap global header encodes linktype 239, so `Packet::createFirstLayer()` instantiates `NflogLayer` and the input is parsed as an NFLOG TLV stream.

coarse_trace.summary: NFLOG TLV parsing reads the padded `NFULA_PREFIX` record's raw length as 5 bytes, advances into the padding, and then skips zeros so later bytes are treated as another TLV.
The shifted `NFULA_PAYLOAD` record is trusted for both `payload` and `payloadLen`, and the claimed payload is accepted as IPv4 without checking that it fits in the real packet buffer.
Packet parsing records the new layer as IPv4, which is the exact protocol bit the fuzz target checks before reading IPv4 addresses.
Because the parsed packet now advertises IPv4, the fuzz target enters its IPv4-only branch and `getDstIPv4Address()` performs the saved 4-byte heap over-read.

fine_trace.note: Source and root cause. On the malformed padded `NFULA_PREFIX` TLV, this line materializes the raw `recordLen` 5 instead of the required aligned size 8, so every later traversal step reasons about the wrong TLV extent.

The reader uses the step-1 size `5` in both its bounds check and its pointer arithmetic. For the padded `NFULA_PREFIX` record that means the next-record cursor is placed three bytes early, inside the prefix padding rather than at the real 4-byte-aligned next TLV boundary.

Because step 2 landed in zero padding, `assign()` skips those padding bytes and reanchors `m_Data` on the next nonzero bytes. The parser now treats later bytes as if they started a fresh TLV header instead of recognizing that traversal had already gone out of sync.

After step 3 hides the alignment gap, the search can continue through later bytes and still return a non-null record for `recordType == 9` (`NFULA_PAYLOAD`). That record becomes the authoritative payload descriptor for the rest of parsing.

The returned `NFULA_PAYLOAD` record is trusted as authoritative. `parseNextLayer()` converts its header into a payload pointer and a claimed `payloadLen` without checking that the value still fits inside the real packet buffer; the saved ASan allocation context shows the backing packet allocation is only 28 bytes.

fine_trace.code:
const iphdr* hdr = reinterpret_cast<const iphdr*>(data);
return dataLen >= sizeof(iphdr) && hdr->ipVersion == 4 && hdr->internetHeaderLength >= 5;
fine_trace.note: This validator checks only the claimed `payloadLen` and the first IPv4 header nibble/IHL fields at `payload`. It does not verify that the underlying packet allocation actually contains a full IPv4 header and destination-address field.
Because step 6 accepts the shifted, overclaimed payload as IPv4, `parseNextLayer()` instantiates an `IPv4Layer` over those bytes instead of falling back to `PayloadLayer`.

On the next parse-loop iteration `curLayer` is the IPv4Layer from step 7, so Packet records the packet as `IPv4` in `m_ProtocolTypes`. This is the exact state the harness queries before calling the IPv4 address getters.
Because step 8 set the IPv4 protocol bit, the fuzz target enters its IPv4-only branch and immediately reads the source and destination addresses from the parsed IPv4 layer.

Sink. The harness retrieves the IPv4Layer created in step 7 and this getter reads the 4-byte destination-address field from its backing bytes. ASan reports that read exactly at the end of the 28-byte heap region allocated for the raw packet in `pcpp::PcapFileReaderDevice::getNextPacket()`.

allocation_context.note: ASan says the crashing 28-byte heap region was created by `new uint8_t[pkthdr.caplen]` at this line.

crash_stack.function: fuzzer::FuzzerDriver(int*, char***, int (*)(unsigned char const*, unsigned long))

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the crash by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42526893 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which produced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4` in `getDstIPv4Address()`.

format.name: pcap with NFLOG packet
format.contract: An NFLOG pcap whose packet TLV stream contains the specific alignment mistake repaired by the staged patch: a `NFULA_PREFIX` TLV with raw `recordLen` 5 followed by three zero padding bytes before later TLVs, allowing raw-length traversal and zero-skipping to disagree about the next TLV boundary and still produce a non-null `NFULA_PAYLOAD` record that looks IPv4 enough for `IPv4Layer::isDataValid()`. The saved ASan trace only proves the resulting raw packet allocation was 28 bytes and the destination-address read overran it by 4 bytes, so the staged artifacts do not justify a broader trigger class beyond this padded-`NFULA_PREFIX` NFLOG layout.
